en: to make a contract; to contract

examples.en: I finally signed the contract for a new home yesterday.
I'm signing a one-year contract with the company.
I'm going to sign the lease for an office next week.
Be sure to read it before you sign the contract.

examples.ko: 집주인과 계약하고 나서 이사 날짜를 정했어요.
examples.en: After signing with the landlord, we set a moving date.
If you sign a monthly rent contract, the deposit is smaller.

explain: 집, 일, 물건처럼 서류와 약속이 필요한 일에 써요. 집을 구할 때는 '집을 계약하다'라고 하고, 계약서에 이름을 쓰는 건 '서명하다'예요. 친구와 가볍게 한 약속은 '약속하다'를 써서 구분해요.
explain_en: It is used for homes, jobs, or goods where papers and formal promises are involved. When renting or buying a home, say '집을 계약하다'. Writing your name on the paper is '서명하다'. A casual promise with a friend is '약속하다'.

examples.en: In elementary school I memorized the multiplication table like a song.
The multiplication table is the first step in learning multiplication.
These days I sometimes mix up the multiplication table.

examples.ko: 구구단도 잘 못 외우던 제가 지금은 수학을 가르쳐요.
examples.en: I used to be bad even at the times tables, but now I teach math.
I made a bet with a friend using the times tables.
The child finds the seven times table difficult.

explain: 한국에서는 초등학교 때 구구단을 외워요. '이 일은 이, 이 이는 사'처럼 소리 내어 외우고, 2단, 3단처럼 '단'으로 불러요.
explain_en: In Korea children memorize the 구구단 in elementary school, saying it aloud like '이 일은 이, 이 이는 사'. Each table is called a '단', as in 2단 and 3단.

en: might as well; if you're going to anyway

examples.en: If possible, please book a bigger room.

examples.ko: 배우는 김에 기왕이면 제대로 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: Since I'm learning anyway, I want to learn it properly.

examples.ko: 기왕이면 같이 먹으면 더 좋지 않을까요?
examples.en: Wouldn't it be nicer to eat together, if we're going to anyway?
As for the gift, pick something practical if you can.
Take photos in a bright place if you can.

examples.ko: 기왕이면 이번 주말에 다 끝내 버려요.
examples.en: Since we're at it, let's finish it all this weekend.

explain: 같은 일을 할 거라면 더 좋은 쪽을 고르자는 마음으로 써요. '이왕이면'과 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 자주 말해요. 부탁이나 권유하는 문장 앞에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: You use it when you mean: if you are going to do it anyway, choose the better option. It means the same as '이왕이면', and people say both. It fits well at the start of requests and suggestions.

examples.en: When autumn comes, I go leaf-viewing with my family.
Many people go to Seoraksan to see the autumn leaves.
During leaf-viewing season the highways are very congested.
Do you want to go see the autumn leaves this weekend?

examples.ko: 친구들과 단풍놀이를 다녀와서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: I went leaf-viewing with friends and took lots of photos.
The leaf-viewing trip was canceled because of rain.

explain: 보통 '단풍놀이를 가다'로 말해요. 같은 상황에서 '단풍 구경'이라는 말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: People usually say '단풍놀이를 가다'. In the same situation they also often say '단풍 구경'.

examples.en: If you follow the person ahead, you won't get lost.
The child follows the puppy.
Go ahead. I'll follow right behind you.
We followed the guide and entered the exhibition room.
While following the ambulance, I got stuck at a light.

examples.ko: 친구가 먼저 출발했고 저는 십 분 뒤에 뒤따라갔어요.
examples.en: My friend left first, and I followed ten minutes later.

explain: 말하는 사람에게서 멀어지는 쪽으로 따라갈 때 써요. 반대로 말하는 사람 쪽으로 따라올 때는 '뒤따라오다'를 써요. '쫓아가다'는 잡으려고 따라가는 느낌이 있어서 달라요.
explain_en: Use it when someone follows in a direction away from the speaker. When they follow toward the speaker, use '뒤따라오다'. '쫓아가다' carries a feeling of chasing to catch, so it is different.

examples.en: The weather is warm today.
The tea I drank yesterday was very warm.
Tomorrow will be warmer than now.
I felt energized after eating warm soup.

examples.ko: 방이 따듯하고 조용해서 잠이 잘 와요.
examples.en: The room is warm and quiet, so I fall asleep easily.
The blanket is warm, so I don't want to go outside.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 함께 둘 다 표준어예요. 온도가 알맞게 높을 때 쓰고, 그보다 센 온도는 '뜨겁다'라고 해요. 다정한 사람이나 마음에도 써요.
explain_en: Both 따듯하다 and 따뜻하다 are standard forms. It is for a pleasantly high temperature, while something hotter is 뜨겁다. It also describes a kind person or heart.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 샤프를 가져가야 해요.
examples.en: You need to bring a mechanical pencil when taking the test.
The lead of my mechanical pencil keeps breaking.
A mechanical pencil is more convenient than a pencil.
I take notes with a mechanical pencil.
There is only one mechanical pencil on the desk.
I bought a mechanical pencil at the stationery shop too.

explain: '샤프'는 '샤프펜슬'을 줄인 말이에요. 안에 넣는 가는 심은 '샤프심'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 샤프 is short for 샤프펜슬. The thin lead that goes inside is called 샤프심.

examples.en: Yukgaejang is a spicy, hearty soup.
I had yukgaejang for lunch.
Green onions and bracken go into yukgaejang.
On cold days I think of yukgaejang.
I ordered yukgaejang and rice together.
This restaurant's yukgaejang has a rich broth.

explain: 비슷한 국으로 '설렁탕'과 '갈비탕'이 있어요. 설렁탕은 하얗고 담백하고, 육개장은 빨갛고 매운 국물이에요. 보통 밥과 같이 먹어요.
explain_en: Similar soups are '설렁탕' and '갈비탕'. '설렁탕' has a white, mild broth, while '육개장' has a red, spicy one. It is usually eaten with rice.

examples.en: The children are playing around in the yard.
You must not mess around during class.
My little brother played around with the puppy.
I broke a cup while horsing around with a friend.
The way they play around is so cute.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 진지해요. 장난할 기분이 아니에요.
examples.en: I am serious now. I am not in the mood to joke around.

explain: 보통 '장난치다'를 더 많이 쓰고, '장난하다'는 아이가 놀거나 가볍게 구는 모습에 써요. 화난 사람이 '지금 장난해요?'라고 하면 놀리지 말라고 따지는 강한 표현이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 화나거나 어이없을 때 상대가 가볍게 구는 것을 따지는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서만 쓰세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you are angry or stunned that the other person is not taking things seriously. Use it only with people you are close to.

explain_en: '장난치다' is the more common word, while '장난하다' fits children playing or someone acting lightly. When an angry person says '지금 장난해요?', it is a sharp way of telling someone to stop fooling around.

en: money bank; coin bank; piggy bank

examples.en: I put coins into the piggy bank.
The piggy bank was full, so I took it to the bank.

examples.ko: 아이가 저금통을 열어 동전을 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: The child opened the piggy bank and counted the coins.
I bought a present with the money in my piggy bank.
My younger sibling saves spare change in the coin bank.
Coins came tumbling out of the piggy bank.

explain: 돼지 모양이 많아서 '돼지 저금통'이라고 자주 말해요. 동전을 모은 저금통을 비울 때 '털다'라고 말하기도 해요. 은행에 돈을 맡길 때는 '저금통'이 아니라 '통장'을 써요.
explain_en: Many are pig-shaped, so people often say '돼지 저금통'. When emptying a full coin bank, people sometimes say '털다'. For saving at a bank, you use a '통장' (passbook), not a 저금통.

examples.en: Our team plays in the final tomorrow.
My younger sibling entered a marathon.

examples.ko: 다리를 다쳐서 이번 경기에 출전할 수 없어요.
examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I can't play in this game.
I met an athlete who competed in the Olympics.
I really want to compete this time.
The coach let me play.

explain: '참가하다'는 모임이나 행사에 두루 쓰지만 '출전하다'는 경기나 대회에 선수로 나갈 때 써요. '대회에 출전하다', '경기에 출전하다'처럼 '에'와 같이 써요. 팀이 선수를 내보낼 때는 '내보내다'를 써요.
explain_en: '참가하다' works for meetings and events in general, but '출전하다' is for going into a match or competition as a player. It takes '에', as in '대회에 출전하다'. When a team sends a player out, it uses '내보내다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is taller than me.
I share a room with my younger sibling.
I gave my younger sibling a little pocket money.

examples.ko: 친동생은 한 명이고 사촌 동생은 세 명이에요.
examples.en: I have one younger sibling and three younger cousins.
I have a junior I care about like my own younger sibling.
I took my younger sibling all the way to school.

explain: '친'은 피가 같다는 뜻이에요. 사촌 동생이나 친하게 지내는 동생과 나눌 때 써요. 그냥 '동생'이라고 해도 보통은 같은 부모의 동생을 가리켜요.
explain_en: '친' means related by blood. You use it to separate your sibling from a cousin or a friend you call 동생. Just saying '동생' usually also means a younger sibling of the same parents.

examples.en: I went up the mountain by cable car.
The view looking down from the cable car is really wonderful.
I bought two cable car tickets.
When the wind is strong, the cable car stops.
Excuse me, where is the cable car boarding area?
The line waiting for the cable car was very long.

explain: 한국 관광지에서 자주 만나요. 남산·설악산 케이블카나 여수 바다 위 케이블카처럼 앞에 장소를 붙여 말해요. 표를 살 때는 올라갔다 내려오는 '왕복'과 한 방향만 가는 '편도'를 골라요.
explain_en: You meet it often at Korean tourist spots. People put the place name first: Namsan or Seoraksan cable car, or the cable car over the sea in Yeosu. When buying a ticket you pick '왕복' (round trip) or '편도' (one way).

examples.en: In the movie, pirates look for treasure.
The kids dressed up like pirates and played.
They say pirates used to appear in this sea.
A pirate ship is approaching from far away.

examples.ko: 해적 이야기를 읽고 바다를 좋아하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Reading a pirate story made me love the sea.
They say pirates sailed with a black flag.

explain: 배를 타고 바다에서 물건을 빼앗는 사람이에요. 허락 없이 복사해 만든 책이나 영상을 '해적판'이라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 허락 없이 복사해 만든 책·영상·음악에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for books, videos, or music copied without permission.

explain_en: A person who robs others at sea from a ship. Books or videos copied without permission are also called '해적판' (pirated edition).

examples.en: I ate pumpkin porridge when I had a cold.
Pumpkin porridge is sweet and smooth, so it's tasty.
I put glutinous rice balls into the pumpkin porridge.
Please pack just one bowl of pumpkin porridge.
The pumpkin porridge went cold, so I heated it up again.
I had a simple meal of pumpkin porridge.

explain: 호박을 삶아 곱게 으깨고 쌀가루 등을 넣어 끓인 단맛 나는 죽이에요. 죽을 만드는 걸 '죽을 쑤다'라고 해서 '호박죽을 쑤다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a sweet porridge made by boiling pumpkin, mashing it smooth and cooking it with rice flour and other ingredients. Making porridge is '죽을 쑤다', so you say '호박죽을 쑤다'.
